transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Adam Chen (Redwood AE), Marisol Vega (Redwood CSM), Priya Patel (Redwood SE); Karen Lopez, Ravi Kumar, Maya Singh, Ethan Park (Solis Health)

Summary: quick QBR / health check focused on usage, cost, and reliability. plan to scope pilot for Dedicated capacity to address cost/latency predictability.

[00:00] Adam Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um, today's the QBR, we'll keep to about 40 minutes, go through usage, costs, reliability, and then next steps. marisol's gonna cover adoption and questions, priya will do the tech notes.
[00:18] Karen Lopez: thanks Adam, appreciate it. we saw some pretty big usage spikes in December, wanted to understand root cause and cost impact.
[00:30] Marisol Vega: yeah, so I'll start with the adoption numbers. overall monthly active routes are up 2.4x q/q, token volume up ~3x, most of the growth is coming from our triage-assistant flows and the clinician-summary job. we flagged a couple of anomalous days — Dec 12 and Dec 21 — where tokens spiked 60% above baseline.
[01:05] Ravi Kumar: the Dec 12 spike was from a batch job that reprocessed old transcripts, that was on us, but Dec 21 looks like an automated retry loop from our queueing system, it kept re-sending the same prompt.
[01:30] Priya Patel: got it. spikes like that, they translate to both headroom and short-term cost surges. we looked at the per-token cost on your hosted usage — roughly $0.018 per 1k tokens with the current model surface, but with inefficient batching and cold KV cache hits it effectively doubles on peak days.
[02:15] Maya Singh: sorry, $0.018 per 1k? that seems low compared to what we're seeing on the invoice. our Dec invoice had a 45% increase. is that mismatch expected?
[02:40] Adam Chen: yeah, so that per-token is the base API unit price. invoices include egress, long-context attachments, and the spike made autoscale create more instances for that window; that autoscale plus repeated calls can create a non-linear bump.
[03:05] Ethan Park: also we've got some higher-responses because we increased max tokens on the clinician-summary step from 1k to 2.5k in November — that change wasn't fully accounted for in the budget.
[03:33] Marisol Vega: right. what we recommend is two immediate levers: 1) re-enable prefix KV caching for the summary flow so you hit warm cache more often; 2) add a short-term rate limiter on the retry queue to collapse duplicates. both should trim peak token counts by ~30-40%.
[04:05] Karen Lopez: okay that sounds good. what's the effort for KV cache? Priya?
[04:18] Priya Patel: minimal for the client side — it's mostly an SDK flag and cache keying. on our side we can turn on a recommended config and send a sample patch. it also helps latency because you avoid re-populating the KV for repeated contexts. note: in the transcript toolkit sometimes people call it K V cash or K-V cache, the docs have that spelled as "KV cache".
[05:10] Adam Chen: quick pivot to reliability — we observed two 5-minute degraded windows last month tied to a regional outage in us-east-1. marisol, can you walk through timeline?
[05:25] Marisol Vega: sure. Dec 15, 11:10-11:16 UTC we had elevated error rates from backend model nodes, root cause was a transient networking high-latency event in the cloud provider. Dec 27 there was a longer degradation tied to a misrouted autoscale event that rolled a few GPU nodes without proper drain. total customer impact was ~11 minutes across the month.
[06:00] Ravi Kumar: we saw about 2% of requests erroring and our frontend retried, so users saw delays. do you have SLA credits or post-mortems?
[06:20] Adam Chen: we do. marisol has the incident timeline and mitigations doc; for anything beyond the SLA thresholds we can look at credits per contract terms. that said, moving to Dedicated would give you SLA-backed uptime and pinned capacity so you don't get autoscale roll surprises.
[06:45] Maya Singh: we're evaluating Dedicated, yes. however security/compliance is a big factor — we need KMS integration for keying and SOC2 attestations. how's Redwood looking there?
[07:05] Priya Patel: we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS and HSM options for Private deployments. for Dedicated we have KMS integration and audit logs. on SOC2, we provided the report during procurement, and marisol can re-share the attestation.
[07:32] Karen Lopez: excellent. aside from cost, performance is top. can Dedicated reduce tail latency? our p95 is 420ms on average but p99 spikes to 1.2s which is hurting real-time workflows.
[07:50] Priya Patel: yes, Dedicated with pinned GPU pools reduces cold-start and tail jitter; also kernel selection we run on the runtime side reduces variance. caching + batching configs can push p99 down ~400-500ms depending on prompt length. if you want strict p99 SLOs we can scope a pilot with throughput constraints.
[08:25] Ethan Park: what about model versions — we saw outputs shift after your default model bumped last month. any guess on how to lock that?
[08:38] Adam Chen: you can pin model versions per route, and we can do canary rollouts. marisol, we should probably propose a pinned model policy for Solis to avoid surprise changes.
[08:55] Marisol Vega: agreed — we'll propose a policy doc. also, on billing optimization — we ran a cost-savings sim using batching and 8-bit quantization on the smaller workload segments; that simulation suggested up to 25% unit cost savings with minimal quality delta for the current prompts.
[09:25] Ravi Kumar: quantization worries us though — do we have regressions?
[09:35] Priya Patel: we can run evals on your test prompt set and give delta metrics (ROUGE, blue-ish metrics, plus human check) before enabling. it's a gated rollout: test, sample, monitor.
[10:00] Karen Lopez: nice. what's the timeline to ship an eval report?
[10:10] Priya Patel: I can run an initial eval within 5 business days if you give the prompt set; deeper human eval maybe two weeks.
[10:22] Adam Chen: ok, next big thing is the pilot for Dedicated. mari, priya — can you outline what we'd need from Solis to scope it?
[10:35] Marisol Vega: from a product/ops side we need expected qps, p95/p99 SLOs, models to pin, and a target cost reduction. from Redwood side we'll propose a minimum reserve and expected throughput.
[10:50] Ethan Park: our estimate for peak qps is 120; average is 35 qps. p95 target 350ms, p99 below 700ms. we'd like to see 15-20% cost reduction at minimum.
[11:10] Priya Patel: that's reasonable. for 120 peak we recommend a 2-GPU reserved pool for the pilot and burst capacity. we'll model expected latency and unit costs and share a proposal.
[11:28] Karen Lopez: curious re: security — can we get isolated networks and stronger audit logging?
[11:35] Adam Chen: yes, Dedicated includes network isolation and we can expose audit logs to your SIEM. Private on-prem is also an option if you need air-gapped, but that takes longer to provision.
[12:00] Maya Singh: any blockers from Redwood's side to start pilot in Jan?
[12:08] Priya Patel: no blockers; we just need the scope doc and a POC contact. I can bump scheduling for Jan 8 or 9.
[12:20] Marisol Vega: i'll own the scheduling and I'll send proposed dates.
[12:28] Adam Chen: ok, quick hit on cost anomalies — marisol will give you a per-route breakdown showing which flows drove spikes and suggested config flags to flip.
[12:40] Marisol Vega: yes, that'll be in the CSV. also included will be suggested batching windows and example SDK snippets.
[13:00] Ravi Kumar: great — the devs will need code snippets.
[13:10] Priya Patel: we'll include SDK patches; small change in the client reduces requests by consolidating prompts into one batch call.
[13:25] Speaker 1: um, there's also the question of multiregional failover — if us-east-1 has issues, what's the failover path?
[13:38] Adam Chen: we recommend active-active routing by region for most production traffic; Redwood supports smart routing with automatic fallback to nearby regions, but for strict consistency you can keep data residency constraints and have a warm standby in another region.
[14:05] Karen Lopez: do we need to change any compliance configs for that?
[14:12] Priya Patel: depends on data residency. we can keep compute regional while shipping logs to central SIEM, or keep everything regional if required. we'll document options.
[14:30] Ethan Park: another roadmap ask — longer context windows for summarization, 128k tokens would be ideal. any progress?
[14:45] Adam Chen: roadmap has a longer-context initiative in H1; we expect incremental support via segmented KV caching and model variants. i'll try to get a rough ETA; not immediate but prioritized.
[15:05] Maya Singh: pricing question — if we commit to a 6-month Dedicated reserve, do we get a steeper discount?
[15:17] Adam Chen: yes, reserved commitments come with tiered discounts. we'll put pricing bands in the proposal; for example, 6-month commit typically gives 10-18% off depending on utilization, and annuals deeper.
[15:35] Marisol Vega: also note we can set up usage alerts and per-route budgets to avoid surprises.
[15:45] Ravi Kumar: good, set those up early.
[16:00] Adam Chen: ok, let's do a quick recap and actions.
[16:05] Marisol Vega: recap: 1) Redwood to send per-route usage & cost CSV (Adam) by Jan 3; 2) SE deep-dive to scope Dedicated pilot and latency modeling (Priya) — propose dates Jan 8-10; 3) Marisol to share incident timeline + mitigations doc by Jan 5; 4) Solis to confirm pilot scope (qps, SLOs, models) by Jan 7.
[16:40] Karen Lopez: confirms. also please include the quantization eval plan.
[16:48] Priya Patel: included. we'll run evals against your test set and share delta metrics.
[17:02] Adam Chen: any other questions?
[17:10] Maya Singh: none from me. thanks for the quick turnaround on docs.
[17:18] Ethan Park: thanks.
[17:25] Adam Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments. bye.

Post-call notes:
- Customer agreed to pilot Dedicated with initial scope to be finalized in early Jan.
- Immediate cost optimizations identified: KV caching, batching, retry collapse, potential quantization on smaller workloads.
- Reliability mitigation: propose pinned capacity for sensitive routes; incident timeline doc to be provided.
- Next meeting: SE deep-dive (technical) targeted for Jan 8 or 9, 2026.
